claim: The Homie convention's current published version is v5.0.0 (released 11 May 2025), superseding the v4.0.0 that Telegraf's homie-v4 layout implements — the spec is actively maintained and versioned
stance_target: if ha-linux-agent adopts a Homie-style self-describing model, it should evaluate v5 rather than follow Telegraf's pinned v4

claim: Homie mandates the LWT: the last will MUST set the root device's $state attribute to 'lost', and a root device going lost marks every child device in its tree lost — MQTT allows only one LWT per connection, so it must be set on the root device at CONNECT time
stance_target: ha-linux-agent's LWT-based availability is the spec-blessed pattern for offline detection; the agent must set its will at connect (exactly what Telegraf cannot do dynamically)
scope_conditions: Homie v5.0.0 specification, Device Lifecycle section
quoted_support: Homie requires the last will (LWT) to set the homie / 5 / [device ID] / $state attribute to the value lost, see Device Lifecycle. MQTT only allows one last will message per connection, but since a device can have children, the LWT message MUST be set on the root device (the device at the root of the parent-child tree).

claim: Homie defines a five-state device lifecycle — init (optional, while announcing), ready (fully announced + subscribed to /set topics), disconnected (must be sent before clean disconnect), sleeping (before sleep), lost (badly disconnected / LWT) — giving consumers unambiguous availability semantics
stance_target: an explicit lifecycle state machine (beyond binary online/offline) is established best practice for MQTT device availability — ha-linux-agent should model shutdown as 'disconnected' and crashes as LWT 'lost'
quoted_support: There are 5 possible state values: init ... ready: this is the state the device is in when it is connected to the MQTT broker and has sent all Homie messages ... disconnected: ... You must send this message before cleanly disconnecting. sleeping: ... You have to send this message before sleeping. lost: this is the state the device is in when the device has been "badly" disconnected.

claim: Permanent removal of a Homie device REQUIRES clearing retained topics with zero-length payloads in order — the $state attribute first, then other retained attributes and property values — because MQTT treats an empty payload as a delete instruction
stance_target: explains the Feb 2026 undeletable-entities complaint about telegraf2hassio: entity cleanup requires deliberate retained-topic clearing; ha-linux-agent needs a decommission path that publishes zero-length payloads
quoted_support: In order to permanently remove a device the following steps should be performed in order: remove the retained $state attribute from the broker by publishing a zero length payload message to its topic. The device will cease to exist. any other retained attributes or property values should be cleared via the same method afterwards.

claim: Homie v5 replaces v4's per-attribute MQTT topics with a JSON $description document (homie/5/[device-id]/$description) describing nodes, properties, children, and extensions; $description may only change when $state is init, disconnected, or lost, and each change requires a new version number
stance_target: a compact JSON description document is a more efficient self-description mechanism than hundreds of per-property topics — a viable alternative for an agent's device manifest
quoted_support: $description yes The description document (JSON), describing the device, nodes, and properties of this device. Important: this value may only change when the device $state is either init, disconnected, or lost. ... version: integer, yes ... Whenever the document changes, a new version must be assigned.

claim: Homie requires all messages to be retained (recommended QoS 2) except controller set-messages (non-retained, QoS 0 for non-retained properties), and empty string values must be encoded as a single 0x00 byte because MQTT treats empty payloads as deletion
stance_target: retained-message discipline is core to MQTT device conventions — an agent publishing retained state gets correct last-known-value semantics on subscriber reconnect
scope_conditions: Homie v5.0.0 specification, QoS and retained messages
quoted_support: The recommended QoS level is Exactly once (QoS 2) (except for non-retained, see below). All messages MUST be sent as retained, UNLESS stated otherwise. ... MQTT will treat an empty string payload as a "delete" instruction for the topic, therefor an empty string value is represented by a 1-character string containing a single byte value 0

claim: Homie topic-level IDs may only contain lowercase letters a-z, digits 0-9, and the hyphen character, with $ reserved for Homie attributes — the same ID constraint family Telegraf's hyphen-substitution collisions stem from
stance_target: entity naming constraints for MQTT topic trees; any agent must normalise host/device names into this charset without colliding
quoted_support: A topic level ID MAY ONLY contain lowercase letters from a to z, numbers from 0 to 9 as well as the hyphen character (-). The special character $ is used and reserved for Homie attributes.

claim: Homie is pure publish-subscribe: controllers cannot query/request a property value — devices must re-publish data regularly as retained messages, and the FAQ explicitly tells application designers to rethink request-reply designs
stance_target: push-interval design is mandatory in MQTT device conventions; there is no pull fallback, so publish cadence is the freshness contract
quoted_support: You don't. The MQTT protocol does not implement the request-reply but rather the publish-subscribe messaging pattern. The Homie convention follows the publish-subscribe principle by publishing data as retained messages on a regular basis.
